lines.japanese: 覚えのある太鼓が聴こえてきて、俺は歩道の真ん中で夜空を仰いだ。
lines.english: A familiar drumbeat reached me, and I stopped in the middle of the sidewalk to look up at the night sky.

lines.japanese: またどこかで、あのハリューとかいう浅黒い肌のあんちゃんが、静かに汗をほとばしらせ憑かれたように黙々と叩いているのだろうか。
lines.english: Somewhere nearby, perhaps, that dark-skinned guy named Haryu was silently pouring sweat as he drummed away with the tireless focus of a man possessed.

lines.japanese: トイレを貸してくれない都会のコンビニをガラス越しに覗けば、文字盤の頂点でまもなく長針と短針が重なろうという時刻。
lines.english: Through the glass of a city convenience store that did not let customers use its restroom, I saw a clock nearing midnight, its minute and hour hands about to meet at the top of the face.

lines.japanese: 方々でいまだ乱暴な光が灯っている。しかし能天気な男や女の多くが巣へ帰ったおかげで、浮わついた街もだいぶ歩きやすくはなっていた。
lines.english: Harsh lights still blazed everywhere. But most of the carefree men and women had returned to their nests, and the giddy streets had become considerably easier to walk.

lines.japanese: この時間になってもまだ駅へ向かわず、千鳥足でなお川下へ向かう連中ってのは、きっと始発が出るまでの延長戦に突入した暇人たちだ。
lines.english: The people still staggering farther downstream instead of toward the station at this hour had presumably gone into extra innings, with nothing better to do until the first train.

lines.japanese: その中にあって、上流へも下流へも向かわず、ただガードレールのそばで不気味なオブジェのように立ちつくす、黒ずくめのでかい女──みたいな格好をした男がいた。
lines.english: Among them stood a large woman all in black—or rather, a man dressed like one—moving neither upstream nor down, simply looming beside the guardrail like some ominous sculpture.

lines.japanese: 舞踏会のお姫様みたいなロングスカート。密林に棲まうカラフルな鳥を思わせる頭。ド紫の口紅はパッと見まるで心臓病患者のチアノーゼみたいだ。
lines.english: A long skirt fit for a princess at a ball. Hair like a brilliantly colored bird of the jungle. At first glance, the deep-purple lipstick resembled the cyanosis of a cardiac patient.

lines.japanese: 他人の趣味をとやかく言うつもりはないけど、その、まあ、なんだ……これはどういうファッションなんだろう。グラムロックと呼ぶには野暮ったいし、ドラァグクイーンにしては華がない。
lines.english: I had no desire to criticize another person's taste, but, well... What was this fashion meant to be? Too dowdy for glam rock, too drab for a drag queen.

lines.japanese: そいつは隆起した喉仏を晒して空を仰ぎ、太鼓のリズムに合わせて静かにオウム頭を揺らしていた。不健康な白い顔の中、アイラインとマスカラに縁取られた目が、一途に音の流れてくる方角を向いていた。
lines.english: He bared a prominent Adam's apple as he gazed at the sky, his parrot head nodding quietly to the beat. In that sickly white face, eyes framed with liner and mascara stared single-mindedly toward the source of the music.

lines.japanese: ひょっとしたらこの男も、さっきのガード下の音楽会に居合わせてたのだろうか。あの場には異様な雰囲気の人種がわんさかいたから、埋もれていても無理はない。
lines.english: Perhaps he too had been at the little concert beneath the overpass. The place had been packed with people giving off a strange air; even he could easily have vanished among them.

lines.japanese: ジェンベの響き。俺はふたたび吠える夜空を見上げた。
lines.english: The voice of a djembe. Once again, I looked up at the barking night sky.

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんー？　どうかしたんですかー？」
lines.english: “Dora? Is something wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、べつに」
lines.english: “No. Nothing.”

lines.japanese: 俺は頭を上に倒したまま、下から聞こえてきた声に答えた。
lines.english: Head still tipped back, I answered the voice rising from below.

lines.japanese: 「はー、流れ星でも見えるんですかー」
lines.english: “Oh. Can you see a shooting star?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、まあ、そんなとこ──」
lines.english: “Yeah, something like—”

lines.japanese: 「身長があと２３センチ伸びますように身長があと２３センチ伸びますように身長があと２３センチ伸びますように」
lines.english: “Please let me grow another nine inches please let me grow another nine inches please let me grow another nine inches.”

lines.japanese: 適当なことを言ったら、すぐに念仏のような早口が続いた。俺は首を地上に戻した。
lines.english: The instant I gave that careless answer, a high-speed incantation followed. I brought my head back down to earth.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、いいけどさ、あんまガチで頼むなよ。お星様引いちゃうだろ。つか滑舌いいな、おまえ」
lines.english: “Hey, fine, but don’t get so serious about it. You’re gonna freak the star out. And you’ve got great diction, by the way.”

lines.japanese: 「赤巻紙、青巻紙、黄巻紙。旅客機百機、各客百人。お綾や、親にお謝り」
lines.english: “Red leather, blue leather, yellow leather. A hundred passenger planes, a hundred passengers apiece. Aya, apologize to your parents.”

lines.japanese: 「うお、すげえ。無駄にすげえ」
lines.english: “Whoa. Amazing. Pointlessly amazing.”

lines.japanese: 「おドラや鳴にお謝り」
lines.english: “Dora, apologize to Naru.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「ちなみにベロでさくらんぼも結べますよー」
lines.english: “Incidentally, I can tie a cherry stem with my tongue.”

lines.japanese: ホーメイは得意げに、爬虫類よろしく舌を出してちろちろ揺らした。
lines.english: Looking smug, Phoenixsong stuck out her tongue and flicked it like a reptile.

lines.japanese: 「いや、でもさ、どうせ願うなら、チャリ見っかりますようにとか願ったといた方が良かったんじゃね？」
lines.english: “But if you were making a wish anyway, shouldn't you have wished to find your bike?”

lines.japanese: 俺が無粋な指摘を入れると、やつは舌をしまうのも忘れてぴしっと固まった。
lines.english: At my tactless observation, she froze solid, forgetting even to retract her tongue.

lines.japanese: そして、お菓子屋さんのマスコット人形よろしく、舌をほっぺたに付けて片目をつぶった。
lines.english: Then, like a mascot outside a candy shop, she pressed her tongue to one cheek and winked.

lines.japanese: 「駄目じゃん」
lines.english: “Hopeless.”

lines.japanese: 「いやー、突然のことだったので、つい欲求のプライオリティに混乱を来たしてしまいましたー」
lines.english: “Well, it came so suddenly that I became confused about the priority of my desires.”

lines.japanese: ホーメイは白々しく言いながら、頭を後ろへ倒した。
lines.english: Phoenixsong tipped her head back as she delivered this transparent excuse.

lines.japanese: 「まー、そもそも星なんて見えないんですけどー」
lines.english: “Besides, you can't see any stars in the first place.”

lines.japanese: 釣られて俺も見上げた。灰色のフィルターに覆われた紫色の天蓋。この街では願をかけることすら許されない。
lines.english: Her movement drew my gaze upward too. A violet canopy behind a filter of gray. This city did not permit even the making of wishes.

lines.japanese: 「なに。おまえ、そんな背ェ欲しいの」
lines.english: “What, do you want to be that tall?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、いえー。いまはまだ、そんな、言うほど気にしてないんですけどねー」
lines.english: “Oh, no. It doesn't bother me all that much. Not yet.”

lines.japanese: 「いまはまだ？」
lines.english: “Not yet?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、だって私ー、これからもりもり育つじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “Well, I'm going to grow by leaps and bounds from here.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、身長と夏休みの宿題は無理な予定立てない方がいいぞ。な、もう育ち盛り過ぎてんだし」
lines.english: “Height and summer homework are two things you shouldn't make impossible plans for. You're already past your prime growing years.”

lines.japanese: 「えぇー、ドラさんは幼女性愛の気があるから、そういう無責任なことが言えるんですよー」
lines.english: “Oh, you can say irresponsible things like that because you have a thing for little girls.”

lines.japanese: 「おい。おい女。おまえ、そろそろひっぱたいていいか」
lines.english: “Hey. Woman. Is it about time I slapped you?”

lines.japanese: 「いいですよー、お手柔らかにお願いしますねー」
lines.english: “Certainly. Please be gentle.”

lines.japanese: 威嚇のために空中で手首のスナップを利かせていたら、ホーメイは笑顔のままさらりと言った。予想外の反応。
lines.english: I had been snapping my wrist in the air by way of a threat. Phoenixsong answered lightly, still smiling. Not the reaction I had expected.

lines.japanese: 「あ……いや、冗談だから」
lines.english: “Ah... no. I was joking.”

lines.japanese: こう見えても俺は、これまで女子供に手を上げたことなんてなかったから、たかがツッコミひとつ求められただけで不覚にも戸惑ってしまった。
lines.english: Whatever I looked like, I had never raised a hand to a woman or child. Merely being invited to deliver one comic smack left me embarrassingly at a loss.

lines.japanese: くいっ。
lines.english: *Tug.*

lines.japanese: 袖を掴まれた。ホーメイは立ちどまっていた。
lines.english: She had caught my sleeve. Phoenixsong had stopped walking.

lines.japanese: 「まーまー、遠慮なさらずいっちょバシッとー」
lines.english: “Come, come. Don't hold back. Give me one good smack.”

lines.japanese: 撫でられるのを待っているペットみたいに、はたかれるのを待っている。つくづく変なやつだ。
lines.english: Like a pet waiting to be stroked, she waited to be struck. What a thoroughly strange girl.

lines.japanese: 「はあ。いいの」
lines.english: “Huh. You're sure?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんならいいですよー」
lines.english: “If it's you, Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: やつは額にかかる前髪を両手ですっと分けたあと、その手を後ろに組んで「んっ」と胸を張った。生意気にいっちょまえの女みたいな仕草だった。こんなときに。
lines.english: She swept the bangs from her forehead with both hands, clasped them behind her back, and thrust out her chest with a small ‘Mm.’ The precocious gesture of a grown woman. At a time like this.

lines.japanese: 小娘はきらきらと瞳を輝かせて、無防備に俺を見上げている。赤ん坊みたいな肌のハリ、額の消えかかったニキビまで見える距離だった。
lines.english: The girl looked up at me defenselessly, her eyes glittering. I stood close enough to see the baby firmness of her skin and the fading pimple on her forehead.

lines.japanese: 俺は不可解な気分になって、手刀を掲げたまま思わず一度目線を外してしまった。我ながらちょいダサ。
lines.english: A feeling I could not make sense of came over me. Hand still raised like a blade, I reflexively looked aside. A little uncool, even by my standards.

lines.japanese: 「どうぞー？」
lines.english: “Go ahead?”

lines.japanese: 俺がもたついていると、やつはすっと爪先立ってさらに顔を近づけてきた。なんだ。なんだ、この状態。
lines.english: When I continued to hesitate, she rose smoothly onto her toes and brought her face closer still. What? What was this situation?

lines.japanese: 「……行くぞ」
lines.english: “...Here goes.”

lines.japanese: 「へへー」
lines.english: “Heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 俺がゆっくり右手を上げると、やつは唇を横に広げてはにかんだ。愛嬌のある八重歯がこぼれた。
lines.english: As I slowly lifted my right hand, her lips spread into a shy smile, revealing a charming little snaggletooth.

lines.japanese: ──ぺちっ。
lines.english: —*pat.*

lines.japanese: 四本の指の腹を置くように、やつのデコを叩いた。ちょっと冷たくて、さらりとしていた。
lines.english: I tapped her forehead as though laying the pads of four fingers upon it. Her skin was cool and dry.

lines.japanese: 「たははは」
lines.english: “Ta ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: ホーメイは両手でそこをさすりながら、まぶしそうに目を閉じて笑う。
lines.english: Phoenixsong rubbed the spot with both hands and laughed, eyes squeezed shut as though against a dazzling light.

lines.japanese: 「はじめてのつっこみ。ひひひひひ」
lines.english: “My first-ever comedy smack. Hee hee hee hee.”

lines.japanese: それから舌ったらずな幼児口調でつぶやいて、とことこ勝手に歩きだした。
lines.english: Then she murmured in the lisping voice of a small child and toddled off on her own.

lines.japanese: 「変なやつ」
lines.english: “Weird girl.”

lines.japanese: 俺は聞こえるようにこぼして、変なやつのあとを追った。
lines.english: I let the words fall loudly enough for her to hear and followed the weird girl.

lines.japanese: 「まー、いーんじゃねえの」
lines.english: “Eh, you're fine like this.”

lines.japanese: 横に並んでも、俺はやつの方を向かなかった。
lines.english: Even after drawing level with her, I did not look her way.

lines.japanese: 「やっぱおまえの場合、いまぐらいのが似合ってると思うけど」
lines.english: “I still think the height you've got now suits you better, though.”

lines.japanese: 「えー？　何がですかー？」
lines.english: “What? What does?”
“Your height.”

lines.japanese: 一文字口にしてそのまま追いぬこうとしたら、やつは短いスカートを翻らせて俺の進路に立ちはだかった。
lines.english: I gave her the one-word answer and tried to pass, but she spun in front of me, her short skirt flaring.

lines.japanese: 眉間に深い皺を寄せ、まるで目の覚める苦いコーヒーを含んだときのような渋い顔をしている。
lines.english: A deep crease cut between her brows. Her face puckered as though she had swallowed bitter coffee strong enough to wake the dead.
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 俺は足を止めざるを得なかった。
lines.english: I had no choice but to stop.

lines.japanese: 「なに、なんだよ。こえー顔すんなよ。つか、口閉じろ口」
lines.english: “What? What is it? Don't make that scary face. And close your mouth.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　ええーっ？　あれー？　えー？」
lines.english: “What? Whaat? Huh? What?”

lines.japanese: 渋面が少しずつ、いつもの呆け面へと溶けていった。やつは首を傾げ、斜め上空どこかを向いた。
lines.english: The scowl gradually dissolved into her customary blankness. She tilted her head and gazed somewhere into the air above us.

lines.japanese: 「んー、おっかしーなー、やっぱり胸キュンするなー。なんでだろー」
lines.english: “Hmm. Strange. My heart went *thump* again. Why?”
“Wh-what!?”

lines.japanese: じいさんから大きな声は控えるよう訓えられていた俺だったが、思わず素っ頓狂な声をあげてしまった。
lines.english: The old man had taught me to keep my voice down, yet a shrill cry escaped me.

lines.japanese: 「んな知ら──知らねーよ。てめ、おっかねーこと言うな」
lines.english: “How the hell should I kn—know? Don't say scary shit like that, asshole.”

lines.japanese: くそ、格好悪いタイミングで噛んでしまった。
lines.english: Dammit. I had stumbled over the words at the worst possible moment.

lines.japanese: 「うーん……そう言えば私、子犬を拾う不良系の話好きだしなー、『ほほえみインサイド』とか好きだしなー。えー、まじっすかー……」
lines.english: “Hmm... Come to think of it, I do like stories about delinquents rescuing puppies. And I like *Smile Inside*. Oh. Could this be real...?”

lines.japanese: しかし、やつはＬ字にした二本指を顎に置きつつぶつぶつ呟いていて、さいわい俺の話など聞いちゃいなかった。
lines.english: Fortunately, she was muttering to herself with two fingers crooked into an L beneath her chin and had not heard me.

lines.japanese: 駅までの道のりをショートカットするため、いかがわしい看板や気合の入った黒服がうろつく通りへ踏みこんだ。
lines.english: To shorten the walk to the station, we turned down a street prowled by fierce-looking men in black suits and lined with dubious signs.

lines.japanese: 朝までコースのお兄さんやお父さんを捕まえようと、あちらこちらで熾烈な客引き合戦が展開されている。一応こんなんでも女連れには違いないから、うざいのが俺に声をかけてくることはなかった。
lines.english: All around us, touts waged savage war for the young and middle-aged men planning to stay out until morning. I was technically accompanied by a woman, so none of the pests approached me.

lines.japanese: テレフォンクラブの店先からは、大音量の呼び込みテープが流れている。お子様の情操教育にはよろしくないが、そろそろ終電を気にしなきゃいけない時間だから仕方がない。
lines.english: A recorded pitch blared from the phone-dating club. Hardly wholesome for a kid, but it was getting late enough to worry about the last train. What could I do?

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんドラさん、あのー、ちょっとした意識調査というかー、念のためのアンケートを取りたいんですけどー」
lines.english: “Dora, Dora? Um, could I ask you a few questions? Call it a little opinion poll. Just to be safe.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。なに」
lines.english: “Huh. What?”

lines.japanese: ホーメイは周囲の景色が変わったことなど気にも留めず、相変わらず思案顔で腕組みしたまま歩いていた。
lines.english: Phoenixsong walked on with her arms folded and her face lost in thought, paying no attention to the change in our surroundings.

lines.japanese: 「えーと、これは一般論なんですけどー、仮に蒼穹女学院在籍中の勉強もできてスポーツもできる身長１４８センチのお菓子大好きな可愛い女の子がいるとするじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “This is only a general question, but suppose there were a cute girl at Misora Girls' Academy who excelled in both academics and sports, stood four foot ten, and adored sweets.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　んだ、その幅の狭い一般論は」
lines.english: “Huh? What’s with that ridiculously specific ‘general’ question?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、仮にですよー？　仮にその万能美少女があなたに好意を寄せてきたとしましょう、ドラさんだったらどうですか」
lines.english: “Only hypothetically. Now suppose this universally gifted beauty developed feelings for you. What would you do, Dora?”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「なに言ってんだおまえ？　ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “What the hell are you talking about? I'll fucking kill you, asshole. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: くだらない冗談だ。俺はいつもの口癖を、いつもより少し多めに盛りこんでみた。
lines.english: A stupid joke. I seasoned my customary phrase with a slightly larger helping of itself than usual.

lines.japanese: 「はー、ぶっころしちゃうんですかー」
lines.english: “Oh. You would kill her?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、まあ、殺しゃしねーけどさ、アレだろ。そりゃアレだ。ほら、よく分かんねーけどアレだから」
lines.english: “Well, no, I wouldn't actually kill her, but it's that. You know. I don't really get it, but it's that.”

lines.japanese: アレアレ言ってるあいだにちょっと考えて、結局くだらない冗談にはくだらない冗談で対処することにした。
lines.english: While repeating *that* over and over, I gave the matter a little thought. In the end, I decided a stupid joke deserved a stupid answer.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあそいつ、何年生って設定なの」
lines.english: “What year is this girl supposed to be in?”

lines.japanese: 「えーと一年生です。ちょうどドラさんの大好きな、少女から大人へと移りゆく過渡期たけなわですね。言わば穢れ知らずのフェアリーです」
lines.english: “First year. Right at the height of that transition from girl to woman you adore so deeply. An unsullied fairy, so to speak.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ待てって、だぁら違げーつってんだろ。俺はフェアリーより、妖艶で大人の色香が漂うサキュバスのような女が好みなんだよ。青くせえ果実は問題外だっつーの」
lines.english: “Wait, I keep telling you, that's not it. I like my women more like succubi—sultry, dripping with grown-up sex appeal. Green little fruits are off the table.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいやー、なかなかどうしてもぎたてフレッシュですよー」
lines.english: “No, no. She is exceptionally fresh-picked.”

lines.japanese: 「だから。もいでねーから」
lines.english: “That's the point. She hasn't been picked.”

lines.japanese: 「ダージリンはファーストフラッシュがお勧めですよー」
lines.english: “The first flush is the finest Darjeeling, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあそいつ、胸とかどんぐらいあんの」
lines.english: “So how much has this girl got in the chest department?”

lines.japanese: 「ふたつです」
lines.english: “Two.”

lines.japanese: 「と誤魔化したくなるようなサイズか」
lines.english: “So little that she has to dodge the question.”

lines.japanese: 「違います。大器晩成という意味です。ちなみに母は大器です」
lines.english: “No. It means the best things take time to develop. My mother, incidentally, is extremely well developed.”

lines.japanese: 「へー。かーちゃん、すごいの」
lines.english: “Huh. Your mom's impressive?”

lines.japanese: 「やばいです」
lines.english: “Dangerously.”

lines.japanese: 「ぼいんぼいん？」
lines.english: “Big and bouncy?”

lines.japanese: 「というか、たゆんたゆんです」
lines.english: “More like lush and swaying.”

lines.japanese: 「したがって、予定では私も２年後にはたゆんたゆんです」
lines.english: “Therefore, according to schedule, mine will also be lush and swaying in two years.”

lines.japanese: 「だからおまえ、無理な予定は立てんなって」
lines.english: “I told you not to make impossible plans.”

lines.japanese: 「無理じゃありません。娘に受けつがれたたゆんたゆんのＤＮＡを信じてください」
lines.english: “It isn't impossible. Have faith in the lush-and-swaying DNA passed down to her daughter.”

lines.japanese: 「つってもなあ、んな想像すらできねーし」
lines.english: “Even so, I can't begin to picture it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それでしたら──ほらっ、ほらっ！」
lines.english: “Oh, in that case—look! Look!”

lines.japanese: やつはいきなり走りだし、ファッションヘルスの入り口に貼ってあったポスターの、肌見せまくりなセクシーねーちゃんをびしっびしっと指差した。
lines.english: She suddenly ran to the entrance of an adult massage parlor and stabbed one finger after another at the poster of a scantily clad beauty.

lines.japanese: 「これ！　これ使って！　これの顔部分だけ、私に挿げ替えてみてください！」
lines.english: “This! Use this! Replace only the face with mine!”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 思わず顎が落ちた。
lines.english: My jaw dropped.

lines.japanese: 俺たちは馬鹿ップルとでも思われたんだろう。店の階段口に立っていた黒服のあんちゃんが、よそでやれよと言いたげな白い目で睨んでいた。
lines.english: The man in black stationed at the stairway gave us a frigid stare that said *take it somewhere else*. Presumably, he had mistaken us for an idiot couple.

lines.japanese: 「いいからおまえ、行くぞ。なんで俺がそんな、思春期の中学生みたいなことしなきゃなんねーんだよ」
lines.english: “Enough. We're going. Why the hell do I have to act like some middle school kid going through puberty?”

lines.japanese: 「いいじゃないですかー、本人が許可してるんですからー」
lines.english: “What's wrong with it? The subject herself has given permission.”

lines.japanese: 「俺が嫌なんだっつの」
lines.english: “*I* don't want to.”

lines.japanese: べちっ。
lines.english: *Smack.*

lines.japanese: さっきより強めに、小娘の後ろ頭を上からはたいた。
lines.english: I swatted the back of her head from above, harder than last time.

lines.japanese: 「てへへ」
lines.english: “Tee hee.”

lines.japanese: やつは今度も、両手でそこを抑えて締まりなく笑う。
lines.english: Once again, she held the spot in both hands and smiled vacantly.

lines.japanese: 「いちいち喜ぶな。マゾか、てめえは」
lines.english: “Quit enjoying every one. What are you, a masochist?”

lines.japanese: 俺は顔をしかめた。ごほっ、ごほん。いちゃついてると思われたようで、黒服が咳払いを始めた。やべえ。
lines.english: I grimaced. *Ahem. Cough.* The man in black had begun clearing his throat. Apparently he thought we were flirting. Bad.

lines.japanese: 体の位置をずらして、俺は恥ずかしい連れの姿を隠した。無言であんちゃんに両手を合わせる。すんません、すぐ連れて帰ります、ほんとすいません。
lines.english: I shifted to hide my embarrassing companion, then silently pressed my palms together toward the man. *Sorry. I'll take her home right away. Truly sorry.*
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 背後からホーメイが俺の服を掴んだ。今度はなんだ。
lines.english: Behind me, Phoenixsong caught at my clothes. What now?

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんドラさん、ふしだらな妄想のなか欲望のまま私を汚しているところ悪いんですけどー」
lines.english: “Dora, Dora. Sorry to interrupt while you're defiling me however you please inside a shameless fantasy—”

lines.japanese: 「汚してねーよ」
lines.english: “I’m not defiling you.”

lines.japanese: 「あのー、なんか黒いひとがこっちをじーっと見てるんですけどー、ドラさんのお知り合いですか？」
lines.english: “—but a person in black is staring fixedly at us. Is he an acquaintance of yours?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 黒いひと──あのアフリカ太鼓に聴きほれていた黒ずくめのオウム頭を連想して、俺は警戒しながら体ごと振りかえった。
lines.english: A person in black. I pictured the black-clad parrot head who had stood entranced by the African drum and turned my whole body around on guard.

lines.japanese: しかし、そんなはずはなかった。そりゃそうだ。俺が叩けるのはせいぜい変な小娘の頭ぐらいだ。あんな気味の悪い化粧男に粘着される理由なんてひとつもない。
lines.english: No, it couldn’t be him. Of course not. The most I could manage was a smack to this odd little girl’s head. I’d given that creepy man in makeup no reason to fixate on me.

lines.japanese: 「あらぁ～ん、やっぱりドラちゃんだわぁ！」
lines.english: “Oh, myyy! It really is you, Dora darling!”

lines.japanese: 黒いひとの正体は、ただの黒いカマだった。
lines.english: The person in black was only a Black queen.

lines.japanese: 「やだ～、このこのぉ！　こんな可愛い子連れちゃって、もう、どこの店の子よぉ、うりー」
lines.english: “You wicked thing! Parading around with this adorable little thing... So? Which club is she from? Spill!”

lines.japanese: 「うるせーうるせーうるせーうるせーうるせー」
lines.english: “Shut up, shut up, shut up, shut up, shut up.”

lines.japanese: 俺はマルチネスが手の甲で叩いてきた回数分、言葉の裏拳「うるせー」で返した。やがてやつは、俺を叩きまくった手の甲を口の横へ持っていった。
lines.english: For every slap Martinez dealt me with the back of his hand, I returned a verbal backhand of *shut up*. Eventually he raised that same hand beside his mouth.

lines.japanese: 「え……？　あらやだ、ひょっとして素人の子？　いやぁねえ、ドラちゃん、早く言ってよ」
lines.english: “Wait... Oh my, don't tell me she's a civilian? Dora darling, you should have said!”

lines.japanese: 「つーかよ？　な、おっさん。もしくはおばはん。俺がいつ玄人の女を連れてたんだコラ」
lines.english: “Listen, old man—or old woman. When the hell have you ever seen me with a pro, huh?”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことより、私これからメンマの店に行くの。ドラちゃんもあとから来るでしょ？」
lines.english: “Never mind that. I'm off to Menma's place. You'll come by later, won't you, Dora darling?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　あー、いや、今日は行けねー。俺、仕事中だもん」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, no. Can't today. I'm in the middle of a job.”

lines.japanese: 「あらあら、素人の娘さんとデートするお仕事なの？　うふふ。いやだわ、ついにドラちゃんも体を資本に……」
lines.english: “Oh, my. Is taking innocent young ladies on dates your new job? Tee-hee. Dora darling has finally gone into business with his body...”

lines.japanese: 「え、いくら？」
lines.english: “Well? How much?”

lines.japanese: 身の丈六尺を越える筋肉質の黒人がいきなり真顔で財布を取りだしたので、俺は「プライスレス」と言いのこしてその場から逃げた。
lines.english: A muscular Black man over six feet tall abruptly produced his wallet with a perfectly serious expression. I left him with one word—‘Priceless’—and fled.

lines.japanese: 「あのー、いまの方ー、日本語お上手でしたねー」
lines.english: “Um, that man back there spoke really good Japanese.”

lines.japanese: 「あー。まあたしかに、上手いか下手かで言やぁキショいだな」
lines.english: “Yeah. If the question is whether it’s good or bad, I’d call it creepy.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんとの接点が想像付かないんですけどー、どういうお友達なんですかー」
lines.english: “I can't imagine how your paths ever crossed. What kind of friend is he?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに友達ってわけじゃねーけど……あー、ほら、学校でさ、遠足の班決めとかあんじゃん」
lines.english: “We aren't exactly friends... You know how at school everybody has to form groups for a field trip?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい」
lines.english: “Ah, yes.”

lines.japanese: 「アレとかってさ、仲のいいやつ同士で組ませると、どうしたってあぶれるのが出てくんじゃん。したら、そういう連中が集まってできる班って、ぜってーあるわけじゃん」
lines.english: “If all the friends group up together, somebody always gets left out. So inevitably there is one group made up of all the leftovers, right?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ありますねー」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah. There is.”

lines.japanese: 「それ。そんな感じ」
lines.english: “That. Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 「はー」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: ホーメイは例によって口を開けて、首を縦でも横でもなくおかしな方向に振った。俺にしては、ちょっと例えが遠回しすぎたかもしれない。
lines.english: As usual, Phoenixsong held her mouth open and moved her head in a direction that was neither a nod nor a shake. Perhaps, by my standards, the analogy had been too indirect.

lines.japanese: 「ま、いいや。いまの忘れて」
lines.english: “Whatever. Forget I said that.”

lines.japanese: 「かいつまんで言うとアレだ、あるラーメン屋の常連仲間。ほら、クレープ屋のパルさん、あいつともそこで会ったんだけどさ」
lines.english: “The short version is that we're regulars at the same ramen shop. Paru from the crêpe shop—I met her there too.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そう言えばパルさん言ってました。ドラの周りには変なやつが多いって。ルイトモだって」
lines.english: “Oh, Paru mentioned that. She said you're surrounded by strange people. Birds of a feather.”

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、各方面に失礼な話だな。失礼な話だなクソババア。ブッ殺すかアノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Hey, that's insulting to everyone involved. Insulting, you shitty old woman. Should I kill that bitch?”

lines.japanese: 「違いますよー、誉めてたんですよー、ドラさんはそういうひと達に好かれる才能があるってー」
lines.english: “No, it was a compliment. She said you have a gift for being liked by people like that.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なんだそりゃ」
lines.english: “What? What kind of gift is that?”

lines.japanese: 「えへー、これ内緒ですけどー、パルさん口ではきついこと言っちゃうけど、本当はドラさんのこと好きなんだって言ってましたよー」
lines.english: “Hee hee. This is a secret, but Paru said that although she says harsh things, she really does like you.”

lines.japanese: 「おい、なんだよ。やめろよ馬鹿。そういうの本人に言うんじゃねーよ。もじもじしちゃうだろコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Hey, come on. Stop that, idiot. You don't tell the person himself. You'll make me go all bashful.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえいえ、そういう意味ではないと思うんですよ。なんて言うんですか、憎めない弟のようなっていう意味でー」
lines.english: “Oh, no. I don't think she meant it that way. More like an infuriating but lovable little brother.”

lines.japanese: 「分ぁーってるっつの。素で解説すんな。まるで俺が思いこみの激しい純情少年みたいじゃねーか」
lines.english: “I know already. Don't explain it like you mean it. You make me sound like some lovestruck innocent who reads way too much into things.”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫ですよー、いつかドラさんにもきっといい人が現れますってー」
lines.english: “Don't worry. One day, I'm sure someone wonderful will appear for you too.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、慰めるとこじゃねーんだよ」
lines.english: “That's not where you're supposed to comfort me!”

lines.japanese: 「うふ☆　もしかしたら、もう天使は近くに舞いおりてる……カモヨ！？」
lines.english: “Ooh! ☆ Perhaps your angel has already descended somewhere nearby... May-be!?”

lines.japanese: べちっ！
lines.english: *Smack!*

lines.japanese: 「はふんっ」
lines.english: “Ahhn!”

lines.japanese: 「お。なんか、だんだんイイカンジの叩き加減が分かってきた」
lines.english: “Oh. I think I’m starting to get the hang of smacking you just right.”

lines.japanese: 「へへー」
lines.english: “Heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 「……なんだよ、気持ち悪りぃな。口閉じろ口」
lines.english: “...What? That's creepy. Close your mouth.”

lines.japanese: 正面に柳木原の巨大な駅舎を臨む、アルバトロスビルのふもと。
lines.english: We stood at the foot of the Albatross Building, with the immense Yanagihara Station complex directly ahead.

lines.japanese: 横断歩道の手前で青信号を待つ群衆の中ほどに、俺たちはふたり並んで突っ立っていた。午前０時を過ぎた駅前交差点には、やけに客待ちのタクシーが多い。
lines.english: Side by side near the center of the crowd, we waited for the light at the crosswalk. There were an unusual number of taxis waiting for fares at the station intersection after midnight.

lines.japanese: 「あのー」
赤信号の中の棒立ちシルエットを見上げながら、ホーメイが口を開いた。微妙に間が長かった。
lines.english: Phoenixsong looked up at the rigid human silhouette inside the red signal and opened her mouth. The pause had lasted a shade too long.

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「兄ともそのラーメン屋さんでー、ですか？」
lines.english: “Did you meet my brother at that ramen shop too?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ……違うけど……」
俺は一言しか答えられなかった。
lines.english: That one word was all I could give her.

lines.japanese: そりゃそうだ。やつのことなんて、実際よく分かってないんだから。
lines.english: Naturally. I did not actually understand much about him.

lines.japanese: 第一、俺がやつに関して語るなら非難一色に染まる。それは血の繋がった身内に聞かせる話じゃないだろう。あんな極道予備軍みたいなロクデナシでも、こいつにとってはごくごく普通の兄貴かもしれない──
lines.english: For one thing, anything I said about him would be nothing but condemnation. You did not say those things to a blood relative. Even if he was a worthless bastard halfway to organized crime, to her he might be nothing more remarkable than an ordinary brother—

lines.japanese: ──あ、でもこいつ、さっきの三馬鹿と顔見知りだったな。んじゃ最低限、兄貴がいい歳してグレてることは知ってるわけか。
lines.english: —Though she knew those three idiots from before. So at minimum she knew her grown brother was still playing the delinquent.

lines.japanese: 考えていたら信号が青になった。俺たちは無言で交差点を渡った。
lines.english: While I thought, the light turned green. We crossed the intersection in silence.

lines.japanese: 最終電車の発車時刻に追われて、駅へ向かう人の群れはみな早足だった。
lines.english: Everyone streaming toward the station hurried, racing the departure of the last trains.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: ゼブラゾーンの終わり際、他に話すネタもなく、なんとはなしにあの男のことを尋ねてみた。
lines.english: Near the far side of the striped crossing, with no other subject available, I found myself asking about that man.

lines.japanese: 「鳳って、家ではどんななの」
lines.english: “What's Otori like at home?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そうですねー。漫然と本読んだりテレビゲームしたりとかですかねー。あー、あとお菓子食べます、それはもうばりばりと」
lines.english: “Let’s see. I read aimlessly, or play video games. Oh, and eat sweets. I crunch through tremendous quantities.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それおまえだろ。俺聞いてんの鳳・兄の方」
lines.english: “That's you. I'm asking about Otori the brother.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、あーそっか……」
lines.english: “Oh. Right...”

lines.japanese: 「……あー、あれ？」
lines.english: “...Oh. Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「んー……あのー、そういえばドラさんいままで、私の名前って呼んだことなかったですよねー」
lines.english: “Hmm... Come to think of it, Dora, you've never once called me by my name.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そんなんどーでもいいから。どうなの兄貴」
lines.english: “That doesn't matter. What about your brother?”

lines.japanese: 俺はむりやり話を戻した。
lines.english: I forced the conversation back on track.

lines.japanese: 「あーはい、どうなんでしょう。分かりません」
lines.english: “Ah, yes. What is he like? I don't know.”

lines.japanese: やつの答えは簡潔だったが、明瞭ではなかった。
lines.english: Her answer was concise without being clear.

lines.japanese: 「なに、分かんないって。おまえら、仮にもひとつ屋根の下で暮らしてんだろ」
lines.english: “What do you mean, you don't know? You do live under the same roof, at least in theory.”

lines.japanese: 「やー、実はいろいろと複雑な家庭でしてー、私が兄と一緒に暮らしてたのって、こんな小さいころまでなんですよー」
lines.english: “Well, my family circumstances are complicated. I only lived with my brother until I was about this small.”

lines.japanese: そう言って腰のあたりに手を浮かせて、眉を下げた。聞いちゃまずいことだったのかもしれない。俺は後ろ頭をがしがし掻きながら、話題を逸らすネタを探した。
lines.english: She held one hand near her waist and lowered her brows. Perhaps I had asked something I should not have. Scratching vigorously at the back of my head, I searched for a way to change the subject.

lines.japanese: 「ところでー、ドラさん、兄とはどういうお付き合いなんですかー」
lines.english: “Incidentally, Dora, what kind of relationship do you have with my brother?”

lines.japanese: 「あー？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 出遅れて先を越された。しかも答えにくい質問だ。
lines.english: I was too slow. She beat me to it, and with a question that was hard to answer.

lines.japanese: 「さー、どーゆんだろーな。いや、俺が聞きてーぐらいだし」
lines.english: “Who knows what kind? I'd like to know myself.”

lines.japanese: 「でもー、とりあえず、あのなんとかっていう兄たちの愚連隊には入ってないんですよねー」
lines.english: “But at least you haven't joined that gang or whatever my brother belongs to, have you?”

lines.japanese: 「愚連隊じゃなくてアレだろ、自警団。私設自警団・柳木原フレイムバーズ」
lines.english: “It isn't a gang. It's a neighborhood watch. The private Yanagihara Flame Birds.”

lines.japanese: 言いながらアホくさくて吹きだしていた。
lines.english: The stupidity of the words made me snort as I spoke.

lines.japanese: 「はあ、よくご存知で……はっ、もしや」
lines.english: “My. You know them well... Ah! Could it be?”

lines.japanese: 「違げーよ、だって、しつけーんだもん勧誘。あ、これは鳳っつーより、むしろその取り巻きがな。もちろん死んでも御免こうむるけど」
lines.english: “No. They just never stop trying to recruit me. Though that's less Otori himself than his hangers-on. Naturally, I wouldn't join them if my life depended on it.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、よかったです」
lines.english: “Oh, thank goodness.”

lines.japanese: ホーメイは胸の校章に片手を置いて、大袈裟な息をついた。
lines.english: Phoenixsong placed one hand over her school crest and breathed a theatrical sigh of relief.

lines.japanese: 「なにが」
lines.english: “What is?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、だってー、ドラさんまで非行少年のひとだったら困るじゃないですか私ー」
lines.english: “Well, it would be a problem for me if you were a juvenile delinquent too.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえがかよ」
lines.english: “A problem for *you*?”

lines.japanese: つーか、縁起でもない仮定だ。
lines.english: What a dreadful thing to suggest.

lines.japanese: 鳳や森里、それからさっきのハゲやらドレッドやら銀髪やらの姿が浮かぶ。生意気盛りの男の子たちは、いまもあの煙たい地下室で精一杯の背伸びごっこをしてるんだろうか。
lines.english: I pictured Otori and Morisato, then the bald head, the dreadlocks, and the silver hair from before. Were those cocky boys still down in that smoky basement, doing everything they could to play at being grown men?

lines.japanese: 「やっぱさ、おまえ的には、兄貴とかがあーゆー系だと困んの」
lines.english: “So does it bother you, having a brother who's that type?”

lines.japanese: 「まー、そうですねー。ひとには言えませんよねー」
lines.english: “Well, yes. It isn't something I can tell people.”

lines.japanese: 不良帝王の妹は、煮えきらない微妙な表情で首をひねった。
lines.english: The delinquent emperor’s sister tilted her head, looking distinctly ambivalent.

lines.japanese: 「皆さん私には優しいですけどー、でもほら、表向きはツッパリのひとじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “Everyone is kind to me, but to the outside world they're still tough-guy delinquents.”

lines.japanese: 「たぶんー、私に彼氏とか出来ないのもそのせいだと思うんですよー」
lines.english: “I think that's probably why I can't get a boyfriend.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、兄貴のことひとに言ってねーなら、ソコは関係ねーだろ。関係しようがねーだろ」
lines.english: If you don't tell anyone about your brother, then he has nothing to do with it. How could he?

lines.japanese: 「うはー、あの映画おもしろそー、全米また泣いてるー」
lines.english: “Wow, that movie looks interesting. All of America is crying again.”

lines.japanese: 案の定やつは聞いてないふりをした。都合のいい耳は家系なのかもしれない。
lines.english: As expected, she pretended not to hear me. Convenient hearing might run in the family.

lines.japanese: 「じゃーなに、アレか。おまえ、兄貴と仲悪りぃんだ」
lines.english: “So what, you and your brother don't get along?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そんなことはないんじゃないですかねー」
lines.english: “I wouldn't say that.”

lines.japanese: ホーメイは駅ビル正面の巨大な映画広告を見上げながら、まるで他人事のように言った。
lines.english: Phoenixsong answered as though discussing somebody else while she gazed up at the enormous movie advertisement covering the front of the station building.

lines.japanese: 「そもそも良いも悪いもないんですよー。あんまり一緒には育ってないですからー」
lines.english: “There isn't really a good or bad to it. We didn't spend much of our childhood together.”

lines.japanese: 「いまはお互い区内に住んでるんで、たまにこの辺りのデパートとかでばったりしますけどー。んー、でもやっぱり『あー』『よー』ぐらいの会話しかしないですねー」
lines.english: “We both live in the ward now, so sometimes we run into each other at department stores around here. Hmm. But even then, all we say is ‘Oh’ and ‘Hey.’”

lines.japanese: 「ソレは仲悪いって言うんじゃないの」
lines.english: “Isn't that what people call not getting along?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そうですかー？」
lines.english: “Is it?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、知らねーから聞いてんの」
lines.english: “I'm asking because I don't know.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、私たちぐらいの歳の兄妹なら普通だと思いますよー？」
lines.english: “I think that's normal for a brother and sister our age.”

lines.japanese: 「ふうん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 俺には妹なんていないからよく分からない。知ってる例を思いだしてみる。
lines.english: I didn't have a sister, so I had no clue. I tried to think of an example I did know.

lines.japanese: タカシと小鳩。
lines.english: Takashi and Kobato.

lines.japanese: いや……あいつらはちょっと特殊か。
lines.english: No... those two were a special case.

lines.japanese: 「あー、でもそうだ。あのー、むかし私が迷子になって泣いてたら、兄が手を繋いで一緒に母を探してくれた記憶とかあるんですよー」
lines.english: “Oh, but I do remember this. Once, when I was little, I got lost and started crying. My brother took my hand and helped me look for our mother.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、だから私、兄は嫌いじゃないですよー」
lines.english: “So I don't dislike my brother.”

lines.japanese: 「へー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 面白い。Ｖシネマの安っぽい悪役みたいなあの男にも、そんな微笑ましい過去があったのか。アレだ。じいさんが言ってた小ざかしい屁理屈。聖者も暴君も貴族も山賊も、みんな昔は乳飲み子だとか何とか。
lines.english: Interesting. Even that man, who looked like a cheap villain from a straight-to-video crime movie, had a sweet little story in his past. The old man used to make that smug little argument: saints and tyrants, noblemen and bandits—all of them had once been nursing infants.

lines.japanese: まあ、だからなんだって話。
lines.english: Not that it meant anything.

lines.japanese: 「うーん……たまにじっくり話してみたいとも思いますけどー、なにぶん兄とは共通の話題がないんですよねー」
lines.english: “Hmm... Sometimes I think I'd like to have a proper conversation with him, but my brother and I have nothing to talk about.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あいつ趣味とか、かなりコアっぽいもんな」
lines.english: “Yeah, his tastes seem pretty hard-core.”

lines.japanese: たしか森里の話じゃ、デスラッシュ垂れながしながらシブサワ訳のサドに耽るのが家での愉しみだとかなんとか。そんなディープなん、この妹じゃなくたって合わせらんねー（実は俺もよく分かっていない）。
lines.english: According to Morisato, Otori’s idea of a good time at home was losing himself in de Sade in Shibusawa’s translation with death-thrash blasting endlessly from the speakers. No sister could be expected to keep up with tastes that deep into the weeds. I did not really understand them myself.

lines.japanese: 「えー、そうなんですよねー。それでなくても他人に無関心なひとですし」
lines.english: “Exactly. And even apart from that, he has no interest in other people.”

lines.japanese: 「無関心」
lines.english: “No interest.”

lines.japanese: あまりに違和感のある評価に、思わず抽出してしまった。
lines.english: The judgment felt so profoundly wrong that I could not help repeating those two words.

lines.japanese: 「無関心はねーだろ。俺にはけっこう積極的にアプローチしてくんですけど」
lines.english: “That can't be right. He comes after *me* pretty aggressively.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そうなんですかー？　あらー、なんででしょうねー。ドラさんってなにか利用価値でもあるんですか？」
lines.english: “Really? How strange. Are you useful to him in some way?”

lines.japanese: 「知らねえよ、本人に訊くなよ、しかも真顔で」
lines.english: “How should I know? Don't ask me with a perfectly straight face.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、そういうのないんでしたら、ただドラさんとお友達になりたいだけなんじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “Hmm. If you aren't, then perhaps he simply wants to be your friend.”

lines.japanese: そう言われても、驚いたり吹きだしたりはしなかった。それは考えたことがないわけじゃない。
lines.english: The suggestion neither startled me nor made me laugh. It was not as though I had never considered it.

lines.japanese: あの無駄に暑苦しい男の言っていることを馬鹿正直に解釈すれば、そしてそれを端的な言葉に置きかえれば、結局はそういう結論になってしまうのだ。
lines.english: If I took that pointlessly overbearing man at his word and put it in the plainest possible terms, that was where it led.

lines.japanese: それは……困る。俺は頬の裏側に出来た鬱陶しい口内炎を舌の先で撫でた。
lines.english: That would... cause trouble. I ran the tip of my tongue over the irritating ulcer inside my cheek.

lines.japanese: トモダチだとかツレだとかナカマだとか、あるいはカノジョだとかそんなの、どうせ無条件に楽しいのは最初のうちだけだ。
lines.english: *Friends. Buddies. Companions.* Girlfriends, for that matter. Whatever you called the relationship, it was only uncomplicated fun at the beginning.

lines.japanese: だったら深入りするよりも、その「最初のうち」ってやつをだらだらと薄っぺらく引きのばしてた方がいいんだ。
lines.english: Better to keep stretching that “beginning” out, shallow and indefinite, than get in too deep.

lines.japanese: 「あのー、多大なご迷惑をおかけしてるとは思いますけど、今後ともうちの翔をよろしくお願いしますねー」
lines.english: “I'm sure he causes you considerable trouble, but please continue to look after our Kakeru.”

lines.japanese: 俺は縦にも横にも首を振らず、言葉ではないげっぷみたいな音で応えた。
lines.english: I moved my head neither up and down nor side to side and answered with a wordless sound like a belch.

lines.japanese: と油断していたら、鳳妹の頭がいきなりぐるんとこっちに向いた。
lines.english: The moment I relaxed, Otori’s little sister whipped her head toward me.

lines.japanese: 「ついでに妹の方もよしなに」
lines.english: “And while you're at it, kindly look after his sister too.”
“...Right.”

lines.japanese: クソ真面目なツラでいきなりそんなこと言われても。
lines.english: How was I supposed to react when she suddenly said that with a dead-serious face?

lines.japanese: 「あら。あらやだ、すっごい生返事」
lines.english: “My. What an impressively noncommittal answer.”

lines.japanese: 「つーか、いや、だってアレじゃん。ヨロシク言われたって、俺とおまえ、基本的にもう会わなくね？」
lines.english: “I mean, what do you expect? You can ask me to look after you, but basically we aren't going to see each other again, are we?”

lines.japanese: 俺は自分とホーメイのあいだで、立てた親指を順に向けた。
lines.english: I raised one thumb and pointed it first at myself, then at Phoenixsong.

lines.japanese: 「べつに、学校とか仕事とか、そーゆー接点ねえし？」
lines.english: I mean, we don't go to the same school or work together or anything, right?

lines.japanese: 「えー、あー、そっかぁぁぁ……」
lines.english: “Oh. Ahh, that's trueee...”

lines.japanese: やつは呆けた声で、いつもより余計に語尾を伸ばした。口を開けたまま、首を突きだすように俯いてすたすた歩く。俺も足元に視線を落とし、舌で頬の片側を膨らませながら歩く。
lines.english: She drew the end of the thought out longer than usual in a vacant voice. Mouth open, head lowered and neck thrust forward, she marched on. I walked with my eyes on the ground too, pushing my tongue into one cheek.

lines.japanese: やがて駅入口に着いた。さあ、これで見送り係はお役御免──
lines.english: At last we reached the station entrance. My duty as escort was now complete—

lines.japanese: ──なんだけど、まあ、乗りかかった船だから。なんとなく俺は、一緒に改札まで付いていくことにした。
lines.english: —but I had come this far; I might as well see it through. For no particular reason, I decided to accompany her to the ticket gates.

lines.japanese: 地下鉄のあの生ぐさい臭いが漂うコンコース。
lines.english: The concourse carried the faintly rank smell peculiar to the subway.

lines.japanese: 自動改札機の向こうに見えるアルミ色の電車へ、柳木原の夜を楽しんできたやつらが次々と吸いこまれている。
lines.english: Beyond the automatic gates, an aluminum-colored train swallowed people returning from a night in Yanagihara one after another.

lines.japanese: 聞けばホーメイの家は風見ヶ丘だって言う。柳木原から急行でふた駅の高級住宅街。いいとこ住んでる。
lines.english: Phoenixsong told me she lived in Kazamigaoka, an affluent residential district two express stops from Yanagihara. Nice neighborhood.

lines.japanese: もしかしたら意外にお嬢なのかもしれない。そう言えば兄貴の方も、金遣いが庶民の感覚ではなかった。
lines.english: Perhaps she was more of a rich young lady than she looked. Come to think of it, her brother spent money on a scale that made no sense to ordinary people.

lines.japanese: でもまあ最寄駅で言えば、俺の住んでるとこだって風見ヶ丘だ。居住地と家柄は必ずしも関連しない。
lines.english: Then again, Kazamigaoka was my nearest station too. Address and pedigree did not necessarily correspond.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 定期入れを探すためにごそごそと鞄をあさっていた途中で、やつはその動きを止めた。
lines.english: Halfway through rummaging in her bag for her commuter-pass case, she stopped.

lines.japanese: 「なに。なくしたとか言うんじゃねーだろうな」
lines.english: “What? Don't tell me you lost it.”

lines.japanese: 「いえあのー、気付いたんですけどー、もしかしたら、パルクレープでまた会うかもしれませんよね」
lines.english: “No. I just realized that perhaps we'll meet again at Paru Crêpes.”

lines.japanese: 「はァ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: なんだこいつ、まだそんなこと考えてたのか。変なやつ。
lines.english: She was still thinking about that? Weird girl.

lines.japanese: 「ほら私、パルさんと約束したじゃないですか、明日から常連になるって。ドラさんもあのお店にはよくいらっしゃるんですよね」
lines.english: “Remember, I promised Paru I'd become a regular starting tomorrow. And you visit the shop often too, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まあ、行くっちゃ行くけど」
lines.english: “Yeah, I suppose I do.”

lines.japanese: 窓口だしな、成田工務店の。
lines.english: It was the front desk for Narita Construction, after all.

lines.japanese: 「ですよねー。でしたらー、またいつかあのお店でご縁があるかもしれませんよねー？」
lines.english: “Exactly. In that case, perhaps fate will bring us together at the shop again someday?”
